# The Noruva AI — AI Assistant

> A real-time meeting and interview intelligence copilot — live audio transcription, resume-personalized context synthesis, an invisible desktop overlay, and low-latency WebSocket streaming.

- Canonical: https://hasib105.github.io/work/noruva-ai-assistant
- Role: AI Systems & Backend Engineer
- Year: 2025—26
- Category: Real-Time Conversational AI
- Stack: FastAPI, Python, Next.js, Electron, Qdrant, WebSockets, PostgreSQL, Redis
- Latency: Real-Time Stream
- Client: Invisible Desktop Overlay

High-stakes technical interviews and client discussions require rapid recall and structured articulation. I co-engineered **The Noruva AI Assistant**: an invisible, real-time desktop companion that listens to incoming audio streams, matches discussion context against personal candidate experience, and delivers live suggestions without breaking conversational flow.

## Real-time speech and context retrieval

The backend pipeline is architected for sub-second turnarounds over FastAPI:

- **Streaming Speech-to-Text**: Ingests continuous microphone and system audio channels, performing low-latency speech transcription and sentence segmentation.
- **Experience-Based Personalization**: Uploaded resumes, project histories, and case studies are parsed and indexed in a **Qdrant vector store**. Incoming questions trigger semantic similarity lookups so suggestions draw directly from genuine candidate accomplishments.
- **LLM Context Synthesis**: Synthesizes structured, concise talking points and code outlines calibrated to the speaker's background, avoiding generic or hallucinated answers.

## Invisible desktop interface & privacy engineering

The client experience is engineered across Next.js and Electron:

- **Undetectable Desktop Overlay**: An Electron overlay application renders real-time suggestions atop video meeting platforms (Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams) with click-through transparency and configurable opacity.
- **Bidirectional WebSocket Backbone**: Streaming tokens flow directly from the FastAPI backend to the desktop renderer with minimal compute overhead.
- **Zero-Retention Security**: Designed with end-to-end privacy guarantees, including configurable automatic transcript purge schedules and an ephemeral zero-retention mode for confidential meetings.

# Torii Immigration

> A guided form-preparation platform for immigration — conversational intake, dynamic eligibility evaluation, auto-filled government forms, and official legal source citations.

- Canonical: https://hasib105.github.io/work/torii-immigration
- Role: Backend & Systems Engineer
- Year: 2025—26
- Category: Legal Tech & Form Automation
- Stack: FastAPI, Python 3.13, SQLAlchemy 2 Async, PostgreSQL 17, pgvector, Alembic, arq (Redis), Next.js
- Architecture: Async SQLAlchemy 2 + arq
- Verification: Official Legal Citations

Navigating visa renewals, status transitions, and immigration filings is fraught with bureaucratic friction and strict legal requirements. **Torii** is a guided immigration form-preparation platform — designed as a reliable "TurboTax for visas" — that guides applicants through the legal process while ensuring strict regulatory compliance.

## Resilient backend architecture

I built the system-of-record API on modern Python 3.13 and FastAPI:

- **Async SQLAlchemy 2 & PostgreSQL 17**: High-concurrency async data access layer handling applicant profiles, case progression, jurisdiction rulesets, and document uploads.
- **Alembic Schema Evolutions**: Automated migration pipelines managed through `uv`, ensuring database schemas stay synchronized across staging and production environments.
- **Background Task Scheduling via arq**: An async Redis worker (`arq`) powers background outbox polling, automated renewal date alerts, and government policy change monitors.

## Automated intake and legal compliance

The platform replaces static PDF templates with an active workflow:

- **Conversational Intake Engine**: Evaluates applicant eligibility dynamically based on nationality, travel history, and visa category.
- **Government Source Citations**: Every generated instruction, required document, and question explicitly references and links to the authoritative government immigration regulation it originates from.
- **Auto-Populated Form Generation**: Validates field consistency across multiple applications, eliminating redundant manual data entry and preventing contradictory submissions.

# Sightline

> An AI-powered exam-integrity review and academic risk platform — automated exam-video analysis, suspicious-event detection with timestamped evidence frames, and at-risk student identification.

- Canonical: https://hasib105.github.io/work/sightline
- Role: Backend & AI Engineer
- Year: 2025—26
- Category: AI Video & Exam Integrity
- Stack: Django, Python, Next.js, Celery, PostgreSQL, Redis, Computer Vision, Docker
- Analysis: Timestamped Video Evidence
- Stack: Django · Celery · Next.js
- GitHub: https://github.com/Hasib105/sightline

Ensuring academic integrity during remote and hybrid assessments requires reviewing hours of recorded video footage without burdening proctors and educational faculty. I engineered **Sightline** as an end-to-end platform that automates video analysis, pinpoints anomalous events, and flags academically at-risk students before the semester concludes.

## Video analysis and evidence flagging

Rather than issuing unverified automated verdicts, Sightline acts as an investigative assistant for proctors and invigilators:

- **Asynchronous Video Pipeline**: Uploaded exam recordings are processed asynchronously using **Celery workers** and Redis message brokers, extracting temporal video segments and keyframes.
- **Suspicious-Event Detection**: Computer vision and audio models detect anomalous events — such as multiple persons in frame, gaze deviations, or unauthorized device usage.
- **Timestamped Evidence References**: Invigilators receive an interactive timeline highlighting suspicious events annotated with exact timestamps, model confidence scores, and frame clips to confirm or dismiss with full human agency.

## Academic intervention and resilient architecture

The platform pairs exam integrity review with early student support:

- **At-Risk Student Identification**: Analyzes student performance trends and submission flags to alert educators to struggling students well before final grading deadlines.
- **Production-Ready Architecture**: Powered by a robust Django API, PostgreSQL relational persistence, and a responsive Next.js frontend, coordinated via Docker Compose and nginx reverse proxies.
- **Automated CI/CD**: Containerized deployments automated via GitHub Actions pipelines with automated schema migrations and model warmup routines.

# Oppora.ai

> An AI-powered sales-automation SaaS built with Django and FastAPI — intelligent automation workflows, multi-model LLM integrations, and production backend services that turn outbound into a system you operate.

- Canonical: https://hasib105.github.io/work/oppora-ai
- Role: Backend Engineer
- Year: 2025—26
- Category: AI Sales Automation
- Stack: Django, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, Redis, Celery, LangChain, LangGraph, OpenAI
- Stack: Django · FastAPI
- AI layer: Multi-model LLM workflows
- oppora.ai: https://oppora.ai

Oppora.ai is an AI sales-automation platform: outbound campaigns researched,
personalized, and executed with AI doing the heavy lifting. I built its
backend on a foundation of Django, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, Redis, and Celery —
the kind of maintainable, production-ready architecture that holds up once
real customers and real volume arrive.

## Automation as a system, not a script

The product is a set of intelligent automation workflows — research,
enrichment, content generation, and assisted execution — modelled as explicit
stages rather than one brittle prompt. Background work runs on Celery task
queues so the API stays responsive while the slow, AI-heavy steps happen out
of band.

## Multi-model LLM integrations

The AI layer integrates multiple LLM providers so model choice becomes a
routing decision per task — quality, cost, and failure handling stay tunable
independently. Orchestration is chained with LangChain and LangGraph, with
structured output parsing keeping model responses reliable enough to act on
downstream.

# SailorSearch

> A search API designed for agents, RAG pipelines, and deep research — it returns clean markdown with enrichment, token compression, and source-aware outputs, so agents get dense, attributable context instead of raw HTML.

- Canonical: https://hasib105.github.io/work/sailor-search
- Role: Backend Engineer
- Year: 2025—26
- Category: AI Search
- Stack: FastAPI, PostgreSQL, Redis, Celery, RAG
- Output: Clean, source-aware markdown
- Designed for: Agents & deep research
- sailorsearch.dev: https://sailorsearch.dev

SailorSearch is a search API built for a new kind of consumer: not a human
scanning links, but an agent assembling context under a token budget. That
single constraint shapes everything about how it returns results.

## Search as an agent interface

I designed the API around three ideas. **Clean markdown** — pages arrive as
structured, readable markdown with enrichment instead of boilerplate-laden
HTML. **Token compression** — results are condensed toward what an agent
actually needs, because every wasted token in a context window is paid for in
quality and cost downstream. **Source-aware outputs** — every claim stays
attributable to where it came from, which is what makes the result safe to
cite in RAG and deep-research workloads.

## Built to scale

SailorSearch runs on FastAPI with PostgreSQL and Redis, using Celery for the
crawl, extract, and compress stages so they scale independently of the query
path — fast responses up front, heavy work in the background.

# Production Tracking System

> A real-time production-monitoring system with predictive analytics and automated bottleneck detection — replacing day-late manual reporting with live signals for operational and management teams.

- Canonical: https://hasib105.github.io/work/protrac
- Role: Tech Lead — Backend
- Year: 2025
- Category: Real-Time Systems
- Stack: Django, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, Redis, Predictive Analytics
- Reporting: Day-late → real-time
- Signal: Automated bottleneck detection

Production reporting that arrives a day late is a report about a problem you
can no longer fix. This system replaced hand-compiled, after-the-fact
reporting with live signals — architected as a high-reliability production
monitoring platform.

## Real-time, on the floor

The system tracks production as it runs and surfaces deviation when it starts,
not the next morning: **automated bottleneck detection** across the line and
**predictive analytics** that flag where output is trending before it becomes
a shortfall. Operational and management teams work from the same live picture.

## Architected to operate

I owned the architecture end to end — Django and FastAPI services on
PostgreSQL with Redis powering the real-time layer — and the data model and
analytics that turn a stream of floor events into decisions teams can act on
in the moment.

# AI Interview Agent

> A conversational AI system for interview simulation — it runs a live interview and returns real-time structured scoring and feedback, turning an open-ended conversation into measurable, comparable signal.

- Canonical: https://hasib105.github.io/work/interview-agent
- Role: AI Engineer — Backend
- Year: 2025—26
- Category: Conversational AI
- Stack: FastAPI, LangGraph, OpenAI, Structured Output Parsing, WebSockets
- Mode: Live conversational interview
- Output: Real-time structured scoring

An interview is an open-ended conversation, but the value of one is in the
structure you can pull back out: how a candidate reasoned, where they hesitated,
what they actually demonstrated. This agent runs the conversation and produces
that structure in real time.

## Scoring a conversation as it happens

The system conducts a live interview and emits **real-time structured scoring
and feedback** rather than a single verdict at the end. The hard part is
reliability — turning free-form model output into a consistent, comparable
schema — which I handle with structured output parsing so every response maps
cleanly onto the scoring model.

## Orchestrated, not prompted

The interview flow is orchestrated with LangGraph as explicit stages — ask,
follow up, evaluate — over a FastAPI backend with a streaming channel for the
live exchange. Treating the dialogue as a graph keeps it controllable instead
of letting one long prompt drift.

# Heimdall

> An end-to-end AI marketing-automation platform — research, planning, and execution driven by agentic multi-step workflows, with humans staying in control of what actually ships.

- Canonical: https://hasib105.github.io/work/heimdall
- Role: Backend Engineer
- Year: 2025—26
- Category: AI Marketing Automation
- Stack: Django, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, Redis, Celery, LangGraph
- Pipeline: Research → plan → execute
- Orchestration: Agentic multi-step workflows
- heimdall.social: https://heimdall.social

Heimdall is a fully AI-based marketing-automation platform: campaigns
researched, planned, and executed with agentic multi-step workflows, and
humans kept in the loop on the decisions that matter. I built the backend
that makes those workflows dependable enough to run unattended.

## Generation with guardrails

Marketing automation fails in a specific way — unsupervised generation at
scale produces content nobody should publish. Heimdall's pipeline runs as
inspectable stages: research, planning, content generation, and assisted
execution, with the expensive, irreversible steps sitting behind a
human-in-the-loop checkpoint.

## The platform underneath

Heimdall runs on Django and FastAPI with PostgreSQL, Redis, and Celery for
background processing. The agentic layer is orchestrated with LangGraph so
each step is an explicit, observable node rather than a black box — the
difference between a demo and something a team trusts with its outbound.

# Architecting Production-Ready Agentic and Computer Vision Pipelines

> Practical architectural patterns for stateful multi-agent systems, real-time vision inference, and resilient RAG workflows.

- Canonical: https://hasib105.github.io/blog/architecting-agentic-and-vision-pipelines
- Published: 2025-01-15
- Tags: Agentic AI, Computer Vision, Backend Architecture
- Author: Hasib Ahmad Bhuyan (https://hasib105.github.io)

Building AI systems for real-world deployments requires moving beyond simple prompt chains into robust state machines, determinism controls, and low-latency inference pipelines.

## State Machines Over Freeform Prompt Loops

Multi-agent coordination frequently breaks down when agents are allowed to run open-ended conversational loops. Structuring execution as a directed state machine provides deterministic rollback points, bounded cycle counts, and audit trails.

### Checkpointing and Human Verification
For sensitive business logic, agents must not execute irreversible mutations without persistence checks. Integrating state checkpointers against transactional databases allows agents to halt gracefully and resume immediately upon human verification.

## Real-Time Vision and Multimodal Pipelines

Deploying computer vision models—whether utilizing YOLO for edge object detection or transformer-based visual representations—demands careful pipeline optimization. Decoupling frame ingestion from deep learning inference workers through asynchronous queue buffers ensures high frame throughput without dropping frames.
